title.narrative: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights in Palestine (SRHR) 2021-2024
Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights in Palestine (SRHR) 2021-2024

description.narrative:
Sverige har beslutat att arbeta mot en mer fokuserad ansats för SRHR i Palestina. Denna ansats har resulterat i att Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS) föreslås implementera ett treårigt program med fokus på förbättrad service och ökade rättigheter vad gäller SRHR i Palestina. De SRHR relaterade behoven i Palestina är uppenbara och Sverige har ett mervärde inom detta område genom sitt engagemang och ledarskap inom områden som kvinnors rätt till reproduktiv hälsa och mödravård sedan 1960-talet, en erfarenhet som kan användas för att stärka SRHR i Palestina. SRHR utgör dessutom en del av Sveriges feministiska utrikespolitik vilket omsätts i handling i och med det föreslagna stödet.
Det föreslagna stödet är presenterat som ett program med en implementeringsperiod om 36 månader med en total budget på 45 miljoner svenska kronor, som kommer att implementeras på Västbanken, i Gaza och i östra Jerusalem. Utöver detta kommer 200 000 SEK att reserveras för att genomföra en granskning av intern styrning och kontroll av PMRS under avtalsperioden.

Sweden has decided to work more towards a focused approach on SRHR in Palestine. This process has led Sweden proposing a program with the Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS) to be implemented over three years, focusing on improving the SRHR services and rights in Palestine. The SRHR gaps and needs in Palestine are evident and Sweden has an added value in this areas as it has been a champion of women's access to reproductive and maternal health services since the 1960's and this experience can be utilized to strengthen SRHR in Palestine. Moreover, Sweden's feminist foreign policy, gives attention to SRHR and this shall be translated into programs and responses to on the ground.
The proposed support is submitted in the frame of a program with an implementation period of 36 months with a total budget of 45 million Swedish kroner and will cover the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem. This is in addition to SEK 200 000 to conduct an internal control review of PMRS to assess the organization's internal capacities.

The proposed program will be implemented by PMRS and will have the following goals:
1- Palestinians, women & men, girls and boys, without discrimination, have access to quality primary comprehensive health care focusing on SRHR and Mental Health and Psychosocial services (MHPSS) service and support delivery.
2- Mobilized and empowered local communities advocating for their SRHR rights with emphasis on youth, women and marginalized groups.
3- A resilient Palestinian civil society has been strengthened.

sector.narrative: Personnel development for population and reproductive health

description.narrative:
2023 According to PMRS' monitoring system the organization has in total reached 1,935,011 beneficiaries during 2023, with 62% being females. Primary Healthcare is PMRS biggest program serving 535,699 beneficiaries through 23 primary healthcare centers and multiple mobile clinics.
There are 15 SRHR clinics across Palestine with a total number of 212,460 beneficiary in 2023. SRHR health awareness has reached 222,056 beneficiaries. SRHR has extensive midwifery services and has provided more than 4,000 cases of postpartum care, including support to victims of gender based violence. Child health clinics witnessed a 61 % increase in beneficiaries than last year ( 58,415 beneficiaries).
To promote access of PHC services to students PMRS operates Youth Friendly medical clinics located in three universities. Overall in 2023, number of beneficiaries in Al Quds university was 33,622, and 7,800 in Palestine Ahlya university and 1,232 in Birzeit University.
In terms of mobilizing and empowering local communities to advocate for their SRHR rights, PMRS held 23 meetings across 3 universities for students covering different areas in SRHR such as breast cancer, family planning, STDs, early marriage and premarital counselling. Psychological debriefing sessions were also carried out to students focusing on psychological first aid and dealing with times of crisis. PMRS additionally implemented 4 student led initiatives focusing on: awareness initiative on Premarital Counselling, Happiness is a Decision Initiative (psychological wellbeing initiative), Mental Health Tent Initiative (Stress Relief Space on Campus) and Nutrition Corner Initiative ( Healthy Diet Orientation for new students) benefiting 1759 direct beneficiaries and 15412 indirect beneficiaries in 2023. Four summer camps were held in 2023 (2 camps for women with a total of 116 beneficiaries and 2 camps for adolescents including 116 beneficiary). Topics covered include genderbased violence and psychological support. Due to the war in Gaza and the violent situation in the West Bank PMRS has increased its emergency operations. With the mobile clinics the staff have been able to give rapid care in challenging circumstances, including movement restrictions. In the West Bank this has been particularly important in areas which are hard to reach. In Gaza over 80 teams have provided primary healthcare, Sexual and Reproductive services and mental health services. There is a close cooperation with UNRWA and the Ministry of Health to ensure complementarity as opposed to overlapping. In this violent situation PMRS must deal with numerous challences, first of all the safety of the staff, resource scarcity and transportation restrictions. Priority is to try to keep staff as safe as possible and to provide fundamental equipment for delivering services
